assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing to ask you to pick Policy 1. This policy says students can bring their phones to school and use them at lunch and in their free time, but the phones have to be off during class.

The first reason is that a ban would be really hard to enforce. Pretty much every kid has a phone, so a lot of people would just hide theirs in their backpack or their pocket. Then the teachers would waste class time trying to find the phones and hand out punishments instead of teaching us. If students know they can check their phones at lunch, they probably won't try to sneak them out in the middle of a lesson.

Another reason is safety. Lots of students have parents who work late, or little brothers and sisters they have to pick up, or a health problem they need to keep track of. If something bad happens, a student should be able to call their family right away. With Policy 2 a student would have to go to the office to find a phone, and that could take a long time. With Policy 1 the phone is right there when you really need it.

Also, Policy 1 helps students learn to be responsible. One day we will have jobs or go to college, and phones will be everywhere and nobody is going to take them away from us. Learning to put your phone away when it's time to focus is something we need to practice now. A ban just puts off that lesson until later. Policy 1 lets us show every day that we can be trusted.

I know some people are worried that phones cause distractions, cyberbullying, and cheating. Those are real problems, and that is why Policy 1 keeps phones off in class. The school could also make clear punishments for kids who misuse their phones, like losing their phone privileges for a week. That way only the students who break the rules get in trouble, and everybody else doesn't.

For these reasons, I hope you will choose Policy 1. It keeps class time for learning, but it also respects what students need and helps us learn to be responsible.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the phone policy. I think you should pick Policy 1, which lets students bring phones to school and use them at lunch and in free time, as long as they are turned off in class. A full ban sounds simple, but it is not going to work the way people expect.

First, a ban is hard to enforce. Almost every kid has a phone. Lots of them would put it in a backpack or a pocket and keep it there. Then teachers would spend half of class looking for hidden phones and writing up kids instead of teaching the lesson. With Policy 1 the rule is easy to follow. If a student knows they can check their phone at lunch, they have no reason to sneak a look during math.

Second, there is the safety part. Some of us have parents who work late. Some of us have to pick up a little brother or sister after school. Some students have medical stuff they need to keep track of. If something happens, a student should be able to call home fast. Under Policy 2 you would have to walk to the office and ask to use the school phone, and that takes a long time when it is not an emergency you can wait on. With Policy 1 the phone is right there in the bag.

Third, it teaches us what to do on our own. In a few years we will be in high school, then college and jobs, and nobody is going to take our phones away there. We have to learn to put the phone down when it is time to work. A ban does not teach that. It just pushes the lesson off until later. Policy 1 lets us show every day that we can be trusted.

Some people worry about cheating, bullying, and kids staring at screens. Those worries are bad, but Policy 1 already keeps phones off in class, so the main problem is handled. The school can also give clear punishments, like losing phone time for a week. That way the kids who break the rules get the consequence, and everyone else is not punished for it.

So I hope you choose Policy 1. It keeps class time for learning, it treats students like they can handle responsibility, and I think most of us would really enjoy proving that. It would be so great, and we will not let you down.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
